title: A gate failure that is the host's is a host fault, not a verdict on the work: not counted, judged again after a backoff, escalated at two in a row, never a halt
prompt:
Read, in crates/spawn-cli/src/integrate.rs, the module comment (step 4, "No room is not a verdict", and the halt rules), `judge_pushed()` (the `rejected` closure and the verdicts, `incompatible` among them), `halt_reason()` and `HALT_AFTER`, `no_room()`, `room_wait()` and `room_backoff()` (the pattern this objective follows), and `aborted()`; `Verdict.output` and `decide()` in crates/spawn-cli/src/gate.rs (what the gate printed, stdout then stderr marked `! `); in scripts/rsi/gate.sh the regression section (`| == regression: <check> must still pass`, the reason `regression: <check> fails on the candidate`) and rsi/scenarios/check-tests.sh (you may not edit them); the errors the `postgres` crate gives a test (its Display, `db error: ...`, and its Debug, `Error { kind: Db, cause: Some(DbError { ... code: SqlState(E57P02) ... }) }`) in crates/spawn-postgres/tests/common/; `spawn_integrator_record` (the verdicts it accepts) and the `task.gated` case of `spawn_control_apply` (`gate_rejections`, `gate_aborts`, the `gate_room_*` fold) in crates/spawn-postgres/sql/schema.sql; `gate_room_escalations` in crates/spawn-cli/src/disk.rs and the digest (`Why`, `Escalation::tag`) in crates/spawn-cli/src/dispatch.rs and dispatch/digest.rs; web/src/components/rsi/Verdicts.tsx, web/src/missionTimeline.ts and web/src/missions.ts; docs/fleet-architecture.md §10.3 and docs/design.md §14. Objective 018 (the resource checks before a gate) is the companion of this one; this one stands alone (it does not need 018 to be solved first).

The problem. A gate that fails because the host failed is recorded as a verdict on the work. On 2026-11-06 the test PostgreSQL crashed mid-gate (its 64 MB /dev/shm: "could not resize shared memory segment", then a segfault and a restart); every database test failed at once with a connection error, and the integrator recorded `rejected` ("regression: check-tests.sh fails on the candidate"): it counted toward the mission's three-rejections halt, the worker got the failures as its own mistake, and the same candidate would have passed on a healthy host. The evidence that it was the host is in what the gate printed and in the test database's own log; nothing reads it.

Required behaviour (the contract the gate checks).
1. When it applies. The gate rejects the candidate with the reason `regression: check-tests.sh fails on the candidate`. The failures are read from the gate's output, in the check-tests section (from the line `| == regression: check-tests.sh must still pass` to the next `| == ` or `| stage gate ` line). check-tests.sh comes in two forms, and both must work:
- the owner's (check-tests.sh is changing to it): first one line per failing test, `| FAILED <test>: <first message line>`, then the excerpt below. When the section holds at least one such line, the failures are exactly those lines (they are complete; the excerpt is ignored for the decision);
- today's: the excerpt alone (`grep -E 'FAILED|panicked|^error' -A5 | head -n 40` of `cargo test`), where a failure is a `| thread '<test>' panicked at <location>:` line with its message (the `| `-prefixed lines after it up to a line starting `| note:`, `| ---- `, `| test result:`, `| --` or a blank one), or an `| Error: ...` line of a test that returned an error. A failure cut off by the 40 lines is not seen; a wrong host fault never lands a candidate (it is judged again), so that is accepted.
Any other rejection reason is judged as today.
2. A failure is the host's when its message holds one of: `error connecting to server`, `Connection refused`, `connection closed`, `server closed the connection unexpectedly`, `terminating connection because of crash of another server process`, `the database system is in recovery mode`, `the database system is starting up`, `the database system is shutting down`, `the database system is not yet accepting connections`, `could not resize shared memory segment`, `SqlState(E57P0`, `SqlState(E080` (a connection error to the test database); or, when the test database's log shows a crash in the gate's window (3), when its message is a database error of any kind (holds `db error` or `Error { kind: Db`). Any other failure (an assertion, a panic of the code under test, a timeout) is the work's.
3. The test database's log. SPAWN_TEST_DATABASE_LOG (new, optional) names a file the integrator can read: the test server's log, lines as PostgreSQL writes them with `log_line_prefix` `%m [%p] ` (`2026-11-06 01:46:58.017 UTC [1] LOG:  ...`; a numeric offset instead of `UTC` is read too). It shows a crash in the gate's window when a line holding `was terminated by signal`, `terminating any other active server processes` or `all server processes terminated; reinitializing` is stamped within [the gate's start - 1 s, the gate's end + 1 s], both measured by the integrator around the gate process. Unset or unreadable: no log evidence (said once in the integrator's output).
4. The verdict. When at least one failure was read and every failure read is the host's, the integrator records `host_fault`, not `rejected`. A real failure among them keeps it `rejected`, as today. `host_fault` is not a verdict on the work: the task stays where it was (`reported`, or `accepted` under review), its `revisions` and `review_note` do not move, nothing goes back to the worker, and neither `gate_rejections` nor `gate_aborts` moves (the rejection and abort runs neither grow nor reset). The record names, besides `base`, `candidate`, `revision`, `scenarios`, `reason` (`host fault: ...`, saying which evidence) and `log` (the gate's output): `evidence` (`failures` when every failure is a connection error, else `server_log`), `failures` (one entry per failure read: `test`, `message` (its first line, bounded), `class` (`connection` or `database`)), `crash` (the log lines that showed the crash, when used), `host_faults` (the mission's count in a row, this one included), `backoff_ms`, `due_ms` and `escalate`.
5. Judged again after a backoff, never halted. A host fault never halts a mission (a halt needs a human; the goal is autonomy), and no halt rule counts one. After the k-th host fault in a row the task waits `backoff_ms` = SPAWN_GATE_HOST_FAULT_BACKOFF_SECS (new, default 300) x 2^(k-1), at most one hour; `due_ms` is the record's own time (`recorded_at_ms`) plus it. Until then no pass runs a gate for it (as `room_wait` holds a task after `no_room`, read from the store's record, never from memory; the mission's other tasks wait behind it as they do there); once it is due the next pass judges it again (with objective 018 solved, its checks run first, so a host still short of room gives `no_room`, not another gate).
6. Counted in a row, escalated at two. The store folds the mission's host faults in a row (a new `gate_host_faults` column, in `spawn_control_apply`: + 1 on `host_fault`; unchanged on `no_room` and `stale`; 0 on every other verdict, on `task.landed` and on `mission.resumed`): a landing or a real verdict ends the run. The `host_fault` that makes it 2 carries `escalate` true (later ones in the same run carry false). The dispatcher's digest takes each such record to the supervisor once, as `gate_room_escalations` does: an item with `session_id` `host` and id `gate-host-fault-<the record's event id>` (tag `host gate-host-fault-<id>`), whose line names the task as `task #<id>`, the mission, the count, the evidence (the crash lines from the log, or the first failure's test and message) and when the task is judged again. Still no halt.
7. Every reader of verdicts knows `host_fault`: `spawn_integrator_record` accepts it; `DELIVERY_TASKS` and the objective history treat it like `no_room` (no step change); the RSI and Missions pages show it as its own verdict (the host's, not the work's) in web/src; the supervisor's digest names it when it lists verdicts.
8. Causality (§14): the decision rests on the gate's recorded output (each failure and its message, named in the record) and on the test server's log lines stamped inside the gate's measured window, both named in the record; the wait rests on the recorded `due_ms`; nothing rests on the reason's text alone or on time without a record.
State the rule in the module comment of integrate.rs (step 4, beside "No room is not a verdict"), in docs/fleet-architecture.md §10.3 (the verdicts, and that no halt counts a host fault) and in docs/storage.md if it lists verdicts. Add unit tests in integrate.rs: the failure parser on both forms of check-tests output (the FAILED lines win over a cut excerpt; one failure, several binaries, a truncated excerpt, an `Error:` line); every connection pattern; a real failure among connection errors stays `rejected`, also when only its FAILED line shows it; database errors with a crash in the window are `host_fault`, with one outside it are `rejected`; the log's timestamps with `UTC` and with an offset; the backoff (5 min, 10, 20, 40, then the one-hour cap) and the hold until `due_ms`; `escalate` only at the second in a row; no halt after any number of host faults; a host fault between two rejections leaves the rejection run as it was. In crates/spawn-postgres/tests/: `spawn_integrator_record` accepts `host_fault`; the fold of `gate_host_faults` (reset by a landing, a real verdict and a resume; kept by `no_room` and `stale`) and of the task. In the dispatcher: the escalation item and its tag, delivered once.

The gate judges this with rsi/scenarios/020.sh (read it). A real `spawn loop` (no model judge) runs a supervisor and four residents of one gated mission on a fake engine; `spawn integrate --once` passes, run by the scenario with SPAWN_TEST_DATABASE_LOG set, SPAWN_GATE_HOST_FAULT_BACKOFF_SECS=5 (and objective 018's thresholds met), judge through a recording gate that prints check-tests.sh's output as scripts/rsi/gate.sh does (in the owner's form or today's) and rejects with `regression: check-tests.sh fails on the candidate`, by what the candidate holds: hostA (owner's form, three connection errors; the excerpt shows one), mixed (owner's form, two connection errors and an assertion only the FAILED lines show), olddb (today's form, database errors that are not connection errors; the log's only crash is an hour old), hostB (today's form with two connection errors, then the owner's form with database errors while the gate appends a segfault and a restart to the log, then accepted). It checks:
- (1) hostA: `host_fault`, gate_rejections and gate_aborts unchanged, the task `reported` with its revisions unchanged, no halt; `evidence` `failures`, `failures` naming all three tests, `host_faults` 1 (and the mission's gate_host_faults), `escalate` false, `backoff_ms` 5000, `due_ms` = its time + 5000;
- (2) the host fixed, passes every half second do not judge hostA before `due_ms`; then accepted, landed, gate_host_faults 0;
- (3) mixed: `rejected`, gate_rejections + 1;
- (4) olddb: `rejected`, gate_rejections + 1, gate_host_faults 0;
- (5) hostB: `host_fault` from today's form (`host_faults` 1, `backoff_ms` 5000); not before its due time, `host_fault` by the log (`evidence` `server_log`, `crash` holding `was terminated by signal 11`, `host_faults` 2, `backoff_ms` 10000, `due_ms`, `escalate` true); no halt; within 60 s a digest tagged `host gate-host-fault-<that event id>` reaches the supervisor, its line naming task #hostB and the crash line; not before its due time, hostB is accepted and lands; gate_host_faults 0, no halt, exactly one host-fault escalation.
On the live main (b92c914; the deployed binary is built from 06cc205) it fails at (1): "(1) task #1, whose every check-tests failure is a connection error to the test database, was gated 'rejected' (regression: check-tests.sh fails on the candidate), not 'host_fault'; gate_rejections 0 -> 1". It exits 0 when every check passes, 1 when an assertion fails, 2 on a harness failure.

Rules: never edit the protected paths, which the gate rejects: rsi/, scripts/ (scripts/rsi/, scripts/blackbox/, scripts/e2e.sh among them), deploy/, all of web/ except web/src/ and web/index.html, rust-toolchain files and .cargo/. The gate also rejects fewer runnable tests than the base (do not delete, rename, ignore or disable tests), any lint relaxation ([lints] tables, clippy.toml, a new crate-level #![allow]/#![expect], a removed #![warn]/#![deny]) and any build-time code (build.rs, .cargo/, a `build =` key in a Cargo.toml). The gate builds offline from the cargo caches already on the host: a new crate builds only if it is already in ~/.cargo/registry. Keep every existing check green (clippy -D warnings, the workspace tests, the e2e, the black-box scenarios, the web build) and add tests of your own for the new behaviour.
